title: fix(deps): pin devalue onto the patched 5.9.2 line (GHSA-9rgm-9g3h-6x36)
body:
Fixes #18930

Clause-②: no

`main` itself was red on the required check `Validate Package Dependencies` — scheduled run `35301766597` (`event: schedule`, branch `main`, sha `36583e989b0b`), failing step **13 — Audit dependencies for known vulnerabilities (OSV-Scanner)**. Every PR whose diff touched any `package.json` inherited that red. The previous day's scheduled run `35176747270` was `success`, so the advisory arrived inside that 24h window; this was never a permanently broken job.

The scanner's finding, read off the job log via the card:

```
| OSV URL                             | CVSS | ECOSYSTEM | PACKAGE | VERSION | FIXED VERSION | SOURCE         |
| https://osv.dev/GHSA-9rgm-9g3h-6x36 | 5.3  | npm       | devalue | 5.9.0   | 5.9.2         | pnpm-lock.yaml |
```

The advisory names a fixed version, so this is the "take the fix" path `osv-scanner.toml`'s own header prescribes. **No exemption was added** — that ledger still holds zero entries, asserted by the gate below.

## What moved

One package. `devalue` 5.9.0 to 5.9.2, plus the override declaration line.

```
 pnpm-lock.yaml      |  9 +++++----
 pnpm-workspace.yaml | 35 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
```

The lockfile diff is 4 hunks / 9 changed lines and names exactly one package. Read from the diff, not estimated: `grep -cE '^[+-][^+-]' ` over `git diff pnpm-lock.yaml` returns 9.

## Remedy shape: the override, not a bare resolver refresh

The dispatch's prior was "take the resolver's own update if it works, reach for an override only if it does not". Measured, that prior inverts here.

`devalue` is transitive-only — no workspace manifest declares it — and is reached through `svelte@5.56.9`, which declares `devalue: ^5.8.1`. That range **already admits 5.9.2**. The lockfile sat on 5.9.0 purely through lockfile inertia: 5.9.0 satisfied `^5.8.1`, so nothing re-resolved it when 5.9.1 and 5.9.2 published — the same mechanism the `hono` note in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` records.

So the resolver route does work, and it was tried first:

| shape | lockfile diff | packages moved |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm update devalue -r --depth Infinity` | 194 lines (107 insertions / 87 deletions) | **12** — type-fest, seroval, postcss, nanoid, picomatch, ip-address, isbot, node-abi, use-sync-external-store, knex, seroval-plugins, tsup peer set |
| `devalue@<6.0.0` override + `pnpm install` | **9 lines** | **1** — devalue alone |

`--depth Infinity` re-resolves the whole tree, so the "smallest change" is the override, not the resolver refresh. The override also leaves a floor behind, which is the posture every other OSV pin in that file documents: a transitive reintroduction lands on the patched line instead of silently re-arming the advisory.

Selector bound sits at the 6.0.0 major boundary per the block's own header rule, never at `<5.9.2`, which would self-invalidate the day 5.9.2 is itself flagged. The selector is floorless because `pnpm why devalue` reports exactly **one** resolved copy in the whole tree, so nothing else is forced onto the 5.x line.

## Evidence

Exit codes captured by redirect, never through a pipe.

Every step of the red workflow, run locally:

| step | command | exit |
|---|---|---|
| Verify lockfile is up to date | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` | 0 — "Lockfile is up to date, resolution step is skipped" |
| Changesets fixed group | `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs` | 0 |
| OSV exemption ledger self-test | `node scripts/check-osv-exemptions.mjs --self-test` | 0 |
| OSV exemption ledger | `node scripts/check-osv-exemptions.mjs` | 0 — "holds zero OSV exemptions (the intended steady state)" |
| Overrides reflected in manifests | `pnpm check:override-consistency` | 0 |
| Declared ranges vs import surface | `pnpm check:vendor-export-contract-resolve` | 0 — "1 edge(s) verified" |

Gate families derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` against this branch; the rest of the runnable set, all exit 0: `check-closing-keyword-parity` (and its self-test), `check-comment-mask-corpus`, `check-prerelease-pin-watch` (self-test and `--verbose`), `check:nul-bytes`, `check:workspace-manifest-cycles`, `check:watch-hint-literal`, `check:driver-memory-census`, `check:refd-timer-probe`, `@objectstack/spec check:llms-txt`.

**The scanner itself: NOT MEASURED locally.** Three routes were tried and each is refused by this container's egress proxy or absent from it — `api.osv.dev` returns `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`; GitHub's `/advisories` endpoint returns 403 ("sessions are bound to their configured repositories"); the `osv-scanner` binary is absent, `github.com/google/osv-scanner/releases` returns 403, and while `ghcr.io` answers, there is no Docker daemon in this container (`dial unix /var/run/docker.sock: no such file or directory`). A scanner binary would not have helped on its own: its vulnerability database lives behind the same blocked `api.osv.dev`. So the before/after scanner verdict is CI's to render, and no local green is claimed. What is claimed locally is the scanner's input: the flagged `devalue@5.9.0` is gone from `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `5.9.2` — at or above the advisory's stated fixed version — is the single resolved copy.

**The advisory's content is likewise NOT MEASURED** for the same egress reason, so severity and fixed version above are read off the scanner's own output line and nothing else.

## Is the bump inert at runtime?

`devalue` is a serialization library, so the question is real. Measured:

- **No workspace source imports `devalue` or `svelte`.** `git grep` for both specifiers across `packages/**`, `apps/**`, `examples/**` and `scripts/**` returns zero matches (grep exit 1).
- Inside `svelte`, `devalue` is referenced only from `src/internal/server/renderer.js`, `hydratable.js` and `errors.js` — the **SSR renderer** path. This repo ships a backend and renders no Svelte components, so nothing reaches it.
- `svelte` is present for two reasons only, neither of them a runtime import: a root **devDependency** that gives better-auth's optional peer-of-a-peer a concrete version to dedupe onto (the existing `svelte` OSV pin's documented mechanism), and that optional peer itself via better-auth.
- The one package whose dependency tree carries `better-auth` to `svelte` to `devalue` is `@objectstack/plugin-auth`. Its dependency closure builds clean and its suite is green on this branch: **112 test files, 2365 tests, 0 failures** (`os-verify-lock.sh` VERDICT `command-exit 0` for both the closure build and the test run).

## Acceptance notes

Observations, none of which meet the filing bar and none of which are touched here:

- `pnpm check:override-consistency` reports two standing selector-shape drifts (`react-router@<8.3.0`, `@sveltejs/kit@<2.69.1`) whose exclusive upper bound sits at or below their target floor. The gate prints these as REPORTS, never failures, and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` already documents them as a deliberate carve-out awaiting a ruling. Pre-existing, not this diff's, and adding a rider here would be exactly the bundling `osv-scanner.toml`'s convention 3 warns against.
- `check-closing-keyword-parity` notes one unregistered file it did not read, `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`, for exceeding its 2 MiB sweep cutoff. That is the gate's own declared behaviour on unregistered files, printed at exit 0.

## Scope

`pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` only. No `osv-scanner.toml` edit — a fixed version exists, so an exemption is the one thing that file forbids here. Nothing published moves: overrides do not ship with published packages and neither file appears in any package's `files[]`, so this PR carries `skip-changeset` rather than a changeset.
